'''LeBron Raymone''' "'''Bronny'''" '''James Jr.''' (born October 6, 2004) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). A consensus four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]], James was named a [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] as a [[senior (education)|senior]] in [[high school]] in 2023. He played one season of [[college basketball]] for the [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC Trojans]] before being selected by the Lakers in the second round of the [[2024 NBA draft]]. He is the eldest child and former teammate of [[LeBron James Sr.]], making them the first active father–son duo in NBA history.

==High school career==
===Freshman season===
On May 29, 2019, James transferred to [[Sierra Canyon School]], a [[private school|private]] [[K–12]] school in [[Chatsworth, Los Angeles]], for his [[freshman]] year of high school. He joined the school with his brother [[Bryce James#Personal life|Bryce]] and incoming senior [[Zaire Wade]], son of [[Dwyane Wade]], a longtime teammate of James’s father.<ref name="pell">{{Cite news |last=Pell |first=Samantha |date=May 30, 2019 |title=Sons of NBA superstars LeBron James, Dwyane Wade to play together in high school |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2019/05/30/sons-nba-superstars-lebron-james-dwyane-wade-play-together-high-school/ |access-date=June 2, 2019 |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]}}</ref><ref name="scs">{{Cite web |last=Fattal |first=Tarek |date=May 29, 2019 |title=Bronny James, Zaire Wade expected to attend Sierra Canyon |website=[[Los Angeles Daily News]] |url=https://www.dailynews.com/2019/05/29/bronny-james-zaire-wade-expected-to-attend-sierra-canyon/ |access-date=June 2, 2019}}</ref> Sierra Canyon's basketball program, under head coach Andre Chevalier, was one of the best in the nation and won the previous two [[California Interscholastic Federation]] (CIF) Open Division state titles.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Gray |first1=Tim |last2=Martin |first2=Jill |title=With NBA bloodlines, the Sierra Canyon boys basketball team is in the national spotlight |url=https://www.cnn.com/2019/12/20/us/sierra-canyon-hs-boys-basketball-spt-intl/index.html |publisher=[[CNN]] |access-date=February 23, 2023 |date=December 20, 2019}}</ref> The 2019–20 team was led by five-star recruits [[Brandon Boston Jr.]] and [[Ziaire Williams]], who transferred there for their senior years.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Cam |date=July 20, 2019 |title=With addition of Chosen 25 5-star Brandon Boston, is Sierra Canyon's 2019-20 roster the best ever? Sierra Canyon went 30–4 on the season and reached the Open Division state championship game, which was canceled due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Sondheimer |first=Eric |title=CIF state basketball games canceled because of coronavirus |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/highschool/story/2020-03-12/la-sp-cif-state-basketball-tourney-no-fans |website=[[Los Angeles Times]] |access-date=February 23, 2023 |date=March 12, 2020}}</ref> As a freshman, James averaged 4.1 points and 15 minutes per game, and was the team's only player to appear in all 34 games.<ref name="freshman" />

===Sophomore season===
On November 12, 2020, James played his first preseason game as a sophomore for California Basketball Club (CBC), a travel team representing Sierra Canyon, against Air Nado, a team affiliated with [[Coronado High School (Nevada)|Coronado High School]], at the [[High School Showcase]]. He scored nine points, all in the first half.<ref>{{cite web |last=Fattal |first=Tarek |title=Sierra Canyon, Bronny James playing as 'CBC' on ESPN2 Thursday night |url=https://www.dailynews.com/2020/11/12/sierra-canyon-bronny-james-playing-as-cbc-on-espn2-thursday-night/ |website=[[Los Angeles Daily News]] |access-date=February 23, 2023 |date=November 12, 2020}}</ref> In February 2021, James [[Meniscus tear|tore his meniscus]] at practice and underwent surgery. Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, he had not played any official games for Sierra Canyon in the 2020–21 season, which was set to begin later that year.<ref>{{cite web |title=Sources: Bronny James undergoes knee surgery after tearing meniscus |url=https://www.espn.com/espn/story/_/id/30965114 |publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=February 24, 2023 |date=February 25, 2021}}</ref> After missing most of the season, James returned against [[Centennial High School (Corona, California)|Centennial High School]] in the [[CIF Southern Section]] Open Division final on June 11. He scored seven points in an 80–72 loss.<ref>{{cite web |last=Williams |first=Brianna |title=LeBron James, Drake and more in attendance for Bronny James' star-studded season debut |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/31615229 |publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=February 24, 2023 |date=June 11, 2021}}</ref> Sierra Canyon, led by junior [[Amari Bailey]], finished the season with a 16–2 record.<ref>{{cite web |last=Fattal |first=Tarek |title=Sierra Canyon's Amari Bailey headlines 2021 All-Area boys basketball team |url=https://www.dailynews.com/2021/06/25/sierra-canyons-amari-bailey-headlines-2021-all-area-boys-basketball-team/ |website=[[Los Angeles Daily News]] |access-date=February 24, 2023 |date=June 25, 2021}}</ref>

===Junior season===
In James's junior season, his Sierra Canyon team was led by seniors Amari Bailey and Kijani Wright.<ref>{{cite web |last=Williams |first=Brianna |title=Bronny James and Sierra Canyon boys' basketball to take on LeBron James's alma mater at Staples Center |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/32781331 |publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=February 24, 2023 |date=December 3, 2021}}</ref> On December 4, 2021, he scored a game-high 19 points in a 71–53 win over St. Vincent–St. Mary High School in the Chosen-1's Invitational at [[Staples Center]], as Bailey was sidelined with an ankle injury.<ref>{{cite web |last=Fattal |first=Tarek |title=Sierra Canyon's Bronny James shines against St. Vincent-St. Mary, again |url=https://www.dailynews.com/2021/12/05/sierra-canyons-bronny-james-shines-against-st-vincent-st-mary-again/ |website=[[Los Angeles Daily News]] |access-date=February 24, 2023 |date=December 5, 2021}}</ref> His team was upset by [[Harvard-Westlake School]] in the CIF Southern Section Open Division semifinals, where he scored four points.<ref>{{cite web |last=O'Donnell |first=Ricky |title=Bronny James has a roadmap to the NBA despite playing nothing like his dad |url=https://www.sbnation.com/nba/2022/3/9/22956487/bronny-james-nba-draft-scouting-report |publisher=[[SB Nation]] |access-date=February 24, 2023 |date=March 9, 2022}}</ref>

Sierra Canyon reached the Open Division regional final, losing to Centennial High School, 83–59, and James was held scoreless while playing through hip soreness. The team ended the season with a 26–5 record.<ref>{{cite web |last=Fattal |first=Tarek |title=Sierra Canyon boys basketball falls to Centennial in SoCal Open Division regional final |url=https://www.dailynews.com/2022/03/08/sierra-canyon-boys-basketball-falls-to-corona-centennial-in-open-division-socal-regional-final/ |website=[[Los Angeles Daily News]] |access-date=February 24, 2023 |date=March 8, 2022}}</ref> As a junior, James averaged 8.8 points, 3.3 rebounds, 2.8 assists and 1.9 steals per game in 29 appearances.<ref name="junior">{{cite web |last=Fattal |first=Tarek |title=Bronny James, Sierra Canyon boys basketball will see top players transfer out this summer |url=https://www.dailynews.com/2022/06/03/bronny-james-sierra-canyon-boys-basketball-sees-top-players-transfer-out/ |website=[[Los Angeles Daily News]] |access-date=February 24, 2023 |date=June 3, 2022}}</ref>

James has been described as a [[nepo baby]], with critics suggesting that his father's influence played a significant role in his opportunities.<ref>{{cite web |last=Granderson |first=LZ |title=Bronny James is seeing the downside of being a nepo baby |url=https://www.latimes.com/opinion/story/2024-07-09/lebron-james-bronny-james-lakers-nepotism-nepo-babies |website=[[Los Angeles Times]] |access-date=January 31, 2025 |date=July 9, 2024}}</ref> After James was selected to play in the [[2023 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2023 McDonald's All-American Game]], recruiting analyst Dinos Trigonis raised concerns about a "smell of [[nepotism]] here that isn't good for our kids."<ref>{{cite web |last=Evans |first=Luca |title=Overhyped and underrated? An inside look at Bronny James' senior season |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/highschool/story/2023-03-28/bronny-james-lebron-sierra-canyon-senior-season |website=[[Los Angeles Times]] |access-date=January 26, 2025 |date=March 28, 2023}}</ref> The Los Angeles Lakers faced similar allegations after their selection of James in the [[2024 NBA draft]], which allowed him to play on the same team as his father despite widespread concerns about his lackluster college play and readiness for the league.<ref>{{cite web |last=Holmes |first=Baxter |title='Set up for failure': What lies ahead for Bronny James and the Los Angeles Lakers |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/41661147 |publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=January 31, 2025 |date=October 8, 2024}}</ref> According to [[ESPN]] analyst [[Bob Myers]], James's agent, [[Rich Paul]], discouraged other teams from selecting him in the draft, threatening to have him play overseas if chosen by another team.<ref>{{cite web |last=Quinn |first=Sam |title=Bronny James threatens, via agent, to play in Australia if drafted by team other than Lakers, per report |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/bronny-james-threatens-via-agent-to-play-in-australia-if-drafted-by-team-other-than-lakers-per-report/ |publisher=[[CBS Sports]] |access-date=January 31, 2025 |date=June 27, 2024}}</ref> ESPN reporter [[Adrian Wojnarowski]] addressed the claims of nepotism by stating that such practices are prevalent in various roles in the NBA.<ref>{{cite web |last=Freeman |first=Mike |title=Yes, Bronny James is benefiting from nepotism. So what? |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/columnist/mike-freeman/2024/07/01/bronny-james-lebron-nepotism-nba-draft/74245347007/ |website=[[USA Today]] |access-date=January 31, 2025 |date=July 1, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Thames |first=Alanis |title=Nepotism debates surrounding LeBron and Bronny James stem from a longstanding stigma in America |url=https://apnews.com/article/nba-lakers-lebron-bronny-4a190e64d3ac7d0abd4f28b4644ea68d |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=January 31, 2025 |date=October 17, 2024}}</ref> James Jr's $2.2 million salary became fully guaranteed on June 29, 2026, one day before his dad announced he would be leaving the Lakers.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Heyen |first=Billy |date=2026-06-30 |title=Lakers make Bronny James contract decision that could signal LeBron plans |url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/nba/los-angeles-lakers/news/lakers-make-bronny-james-contract-decision-signal-lebron-plans/c358b0b78b807fb287d4c130 |access-date=2026-07-01 |website=Sporting News |language=en-us}}</ref>

==Personal life==
[[File:Miami Heat Championship Parade 2012 3.jpg|thumb|Bronny with his father [[LeBron James|LeBron]] (left) and mother Savannah (right) during the [[Miami Heat]]'s 2012 NBA champions title celebration]]
James's godfather is NBA All-Star [[Chris Paul]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cwik |first=Chris |date=March 5, 2018 |title=LeBron James Jr. put on a dominant show with godfather Chris Paul watching |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/lebron-james-jr-put-dominant-show-godfather-chris-paul-watching-054004587.html |access-date=July 31, 2018 |publisher=[[Yahoo Sports]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Chris Paul Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft Status and more |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/p/paulch01.html |access-date=2024-06-29 |website=[[Sports Reference|Basketball Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> who is a close friend of his father.<ref>{{cite web |last=Helin |first=Kurt |title=LeBron helping Chris Paul count down wins left until NBA title |url=https://nba.nbcsports.com/2021/07/09/lebron-helping-chris-paul-count-down-wins-left-until-nba-title/ |publisher=[[NBC Sports]] |access-date=May 9, 2023 |date=July 9, 2021}}</ref>

In 2020, James signed with [[esports]] organization [[FaZe Clan]]. Through the partnership, he was expected to stream ''[[Fortnite]]'' and ''[[Call of Duty: Warzone (2020 video game)|Call of Duty: Warzone]]'' under the handle "FaZe Bronny."<ref>{{cite magazine |title=Bronny James, LeBron's Son, Joins Professional Esports Organization |url=https://www.si.com/more-sports/2020/08/31/bronny-james-joins-pro-esports-organization |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=May 9, 2023 |date=August 30, 2020}}</ref> In June 2021, James made his first appearance on the cover of ''[[Sports Illustrated]]'' alongside members of FaZe Clan, including [[NFL]] quarterback [[Kyler Murray]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Singh |first=Sanjesh |title=Bronny James makes first cover of Sports Illustrated with FaZe Clan |url=https://lebronwire.usatoday.com/2021/06/10/bronny-james-makes-first-cover-of-sports-illustrated-with-faze-clan/ |publisher=LeBron Wire |access-date=May 9, 2023 |date=June 10, 2021}}</ref>

James has established a large [[social media]] following since high school.<ref>{{cite web |last=Smith |first=KJ |title=World's most influential teenage basketball players |url=https://www.on3.com/news/worlds-most-influential-teenage-basketball-players/ |publisher=On3 |access-date=May 9, 2023 |date=August 18, 2021}}</ref> In May 2019, he started an [[Instagram]] account and reached one million followers in his first day on the platform.<ref>{{cite web |last=Baer |first=Jack |title=Bronny James rants about girls and weed, gets smack-talked by Draymond Green in first day on Instagram |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/lebron-james-bronny-instagram-followers-draymond-green-041030248.html |publisher=[[Yahoo! Sports]] |access-date=May 9, 2023 |date=May 29, 2019}}</ref> By the end of high school, James had over seven million followers on Instagram.<ref>{{cite news|last=Zagoria |first=Adam |title=Bronny James Commits to U.S.C. as Father Dreams of N.B.A. Meet-Up |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2023/05/07/sports/basketball/bronny-lebron-james-usc.html |work=[[The New York Times]] |access-date=May 9, 2023 |date=May 7, 2023}}</ref>

Analysts projected James to have one of the highest-earning potentials from his [[Student athlete compensation|name, image and likeness]] (NIL) among college athletes.<ref>{{cite web |last=Pope |first=Keegan |title=Bronny James tops NIL valuation projections from On3 |url=https://www.on3.com/nil/news/bronny-james-tops-nil-valuation-projections-from-on3/ |publisher=On3 |access-date=May 9, 2023 |date=May 6, 2023}}</ref> In February 2022, he filed for trademarks on variations of his name: Bronny, BJ Jr. and Bronald.<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Pickman |first=Ben |title=LeBron James Jr. Files Three Trademarks for Variety of Names |url=https://www.si.com/extra-mustard/2022/02/02/bronny-james-files-trademark-names |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=May 9, 2023 |date=February 2, 2022}}</ref> In high school, James signed NIL deals with [[Nike, Inc.|Nike]] and [[Beats Electronics|Beats by Dre]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Greer |first=Jordan |title=Bronny James' NIL deals, explained: Nike, Beats by Dre among brands teaming up with LeBron's son |url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/nba/news/bronny-james-nil-deals-nike-beats-by-dre-lebron-son/wnbonsmou3k1gmkrk5eixtoq |website=[[The Sporting News]] |access-date=May 9, 2023 |date=March 28, 2023}}</ref>

===Basketball jersey number===
James has worn the number 0 jersey because it is the number worn by his favorite NBA player, [[Russell Westbrook]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bohlin |first=Michael |date=February 17, 2018 |title=Russell Westbrook plays one-on-one with LeBron James Jr. |url=https://247sports.com/nba/cleveland-cavaliers/article/russell-westbrook-plays-one-on-one-with-lebron-james-jr-115246380/ |access-date=August 1, 2018 |publisher=[[247Sports]]}}</ref> He has also worn the number 23 jersey in honor of his father.<ref name=number23/> In July 2024, James chose the number 9 jersey for his professional debut in the NBA during the [[2024–25 Los Angeles Lakers season]]. The decision was made to honor the late musician [[Juice Wrld]], alluding to Juice's 2017 debut EP ''[[Juice Wrld discography#EPs|9 9 9]]''.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.vibe.com/news/sports/bronny-james-homage-juice-wrld-los-angeles-lakers-jersey-1234891503/ | website=vibe.com| title= Bronny James Pays Homage To Juice WRLD With Los Angeles Lakers Jersey Number|first=Marc|last=Griffin|language=en-US|date=3 July 2024| access-date=30 September 2024}}</ref>
